claims.text: Extending the ageing period at an optimized annealing temperature enhances toughness retention in high-entropy alloys.
The enhanced toughness retention results from the formation and stabilization of nanoscale precipitates.
Standard solid-solution processing such as arc melting can produce a homogeneous high-entropy-alloy microstructure before post-processing.
Increasing ageing time at a fixed annealing temperature is the controlled processing change proposed relative to the standard treatment.
A temperature window around 800–1000 °C is critical or optimized for the proposed treatment.
Controlled cooling rates influence precipitate formation.
The relevant structural mediator is the nucleation, growth, and spatial distribution of nanoscale precipitates.
Extended ageing at an optimal temperature enhances the formation and stabilization of coherent nanoscale precipitates.
Coherent nanoscale precipitates act as barriers to crack propagation.
Precipitate evolution governs the alloy's ability to retain toughness under mechanical stress.
The modified treatment will produce a higher nanoscale-precipitate density than the baseline treatment.
The modified treatment will produce a more uniform nanoscale-precipitate dispersion than the baseline treatment.
Increased precipitate density and uniformity will correlate with higher measured fracture toughness.
The proposed behavior applies to high-entropy alloys having similar compositional complexity and phase stability within the specified processing-temperature range.
Markedly different compositions or processing outside the stated temperature range may alter the proposed effects.
The quantitative relationship among ageing time, precipitate size, coherence, distribution, and toughness retention is not established.
